research_concepts: primary defensive matchup stability across seasons
methodological_questions: Is each star's top sequential suppressor stable across seasons?
How is a teammate X->Y sequence premium defined and estimated against a baseline?
What per-cell sample size is needed for a stable suppression estimate, given n=20 per player-season-opponent?
How is season-to-season reliability measured, and how is regression to the mean handled when picking the top suppressor?
Which confounders (role, minutes, opponent quality, lineup, shot distance) affect suppression and sequence premiums?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval tool returned no study-family records for this question, so no prior finding from this project is available to rely on.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether top sequential suppressors are stable across seasons.
Whether any teammate X->Y sequence has a reliable negative premium.
Whether a sample of n=20 per player-season-opponent is adequate for either estimate.
Any reliability, power, or confounding result for this data.
own_inferences: The 'top suppressor' is chosen from many candidate defenders or sequences. Picking the maximum on one season and checking it on another will be biased upward by regression to the mean unless the selection is cross-validated across seasons.
Per-cell counts with n=20 are likely too small for stable sequential suppression rates, so shrinkage or hierarchical pooling is needed.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial as of 2026-05-31 and should be excluded from any analysis dated to that day.
The 'best/avoid' counter-strategy framing goes beyond a stability claim. A stability test does not show that exploiting a suppressor or avoiding a sequence would improve outcomes.
uncertainties: The unit 'n=20' is not defined in the task (possessions, games, or matchup instances), so effective sample size is unknown.
The exact premium formula, baseline, and minimum-count threshold for X->Y sequences are not specified.
Derived play-type labels from the graph database may carry labelling error, and their validity is unverified.
Roster and role changes across seasons may break the stability comparison.
No prior work was retrieved, so whether the question has been answered before is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned an empty list, so no earlier findings, failed approaches, or statuses were available. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone.

blocking_constraints.text: n=20 per player-season-opponent gives low power for stable suppression rates and for sparse X->Y sequence premiums.
Teammate X->Y sequences are rare, so many pairs will have too few possessions to estimate a premium.
Selecting each star's top suppressor and then testing stability reuses the same data and inflates apparent stability.
Season-to-season reliability of the suppression metric is unknown and may be low.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was returned by the retrieval tool, so no prior study can be cited and whether this question has already been answered is unknown.

risks.text: Small per-cell samples give wide intervals on suppression rates; stability correlations may be underpowered.
Many X->Y pairs lack enough shared possessions, so premium estimates are unstable or missing for most pairs.
Top-suppressor selection on the same seasons inflates the stability estimate through regression to the mean.
Searching over many defenders and sequences for the most negative premium yields false positives without correction.
Suppression and premium metrics may have low split-half or year-to-year reliability, so stability may be an artifact of noise.
Opponent quality, role, minutes, lineup, and shot distance may drive apparent suppression or premiums.
Play-type labels and points are derived from outcomes, so sequence premiums may partly reflect the outcome being predicted.
Play-by-play action and sub-type labels and derived play-type records may be mislabelled, biasing sequence attribution.
Rule changes, roster turnover, and coaching changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make seasons non-comparable.
Using 2025-26 playoff data before it is complete, or future seasons to select suppressors, leaks information.

design.estimand: Season-to-season reliability (ICC and rank correlation) of each star's top sequential suppression metric, and the shrunken mean premium of teammate X->Y sequences relative to a matched baseline.
design.unit: Defender-season for suppression, and teammate-pair-season for premiums, built from individual possessions in play-by-play.
design.sample: Regular-season data for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (the 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial as of 2026-05-31. Restrict to defender-seasons and pairs above a preregistered possession minimum.
design.power: Compute power by simulation from the observed per-cell variance before running the study. Report the minimum detectable ICC and premium. If the simulated power is low, report the estimates as descriptive only.
design.controls: Adjust for opponent quality, minutes, starter status, lineup, and shot distance mix using hierarchical shrinkage, with player and team random effects. Define the baseline for each premium before analysis.
design.falsification: Permute season labels and teammate assignments to build a null distribution for top-suppressor stability and for the most negative premium. Use a pre-registered placebo season (for example, an unrelated stat) as a negative control.
design.multiplicity: Apply false discovery rate control (Benjamini-Hochberg) across all candidate defenders and pairs. Select the top suppressor on one season set and evaluate stability on a held-out season set.
design.decision_rule: Call stability supported only if the cross-validated ICC or rank correlation exceeds a preregistered threshold and its interval excludes the permutation null. Call a premium supported only if the shrunken premium survives FDR control and the held-out season check. Otherwise report inconclusive. Do not make best/avoid counter-strategy recommendations from these results.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons; 2025-26 regular season used only as complete data from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded as partial; derived play-type graph records versioned and frozen before analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-31, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Each star's top sequential suppressor is stable across seasons, and some teammate X->Y sequences have large negative premiums.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=20 per player-season-opp; n=20

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
